standard.title: Text language features by purpose
standard.description: describe how texts across the curriculum use different language features and structures to serve their purpose
standard.prior_knowledge: Students identify how texts across the curriculum are organised differently depending on purpose (AC9E2LA03). They have not yet described the specific language features — as distinct from structures — that serve each text type's purpose.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe how texts across the curriculum use specific language features and structures to serve their purpose.

nodes.label: Structure and language features of factual texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the typical structure and language features of factual text types including recounts, autobiographies, procedures and reports.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the structure and at least two language features of one factual text type (e.g. recount, procedure, report) and explain how they serve the text's purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Describe the typical text structure and language features of factual recounts, autobiographies, procedures and reports — connecting each structural stage and language feature to the text's purpose.
wider: Compare language features across two factual text types with different purposes (e.g. procedure vs report) and explain why different features are needed
Identify a text that mixes features from more than one text type and discuss why the author might have made those choices

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate descriptions of multiple text types before they can generalise about how purpose drives structural and language choices. Building a repertoire across factual text types is the prerequisite for the comparative understanding the descriptor targets.

success_criteria: Student names the structure of a factual text type (its stages/sections)
Student identifies at least two language features of that text type and connects each to the text's purpose

nodes.label: Structure of arguments
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the stages of a basic argument structure (introduction, arguments, conclusion) and describe the language features that support each stage.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the introduction, at least one argument and the conclusion in a simple persuasive text, and describe one language feature in any stage.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe the stages of a basic argument (introduction, argument 1, argument 2, conclusion) and the language features that signal and support each stage.
wider: Compare the argument structure in a children's persuasive text with a media advertisement, identifying what differs and discussing why
Write a simple argument using the identified structure and language features, then check whether each stage does its job

response_modes.reason: Argument structure is a reasoning scaffold as much as a text structure at Y3 — students need to understand what each stage does (state position, give evidence, restate) before the structure becomes usable for reading and writing.

success_criteria: Student identifies at least two stages of a basic argument in a text
Student describes at least one language feature in a named stage and connects it to what that stage is trying to do
